title: Basic Error Catching
description: Use TRY/EXCEPT to catch and handle a failing operation without crashing the test.

theory.title: Exercise 3.2.1: Basic TRY/EXCEPT
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "When operations might fail, we use TRY/EXCEPT. Think of it like a safety net—if something goes wrong in the TRY block, the EXCEPT block catches it."

TRY/EXCEPT Error Handling

TRY/EXCEPT blocks catch errors and handle them gracefully:

TRY
    # Code that might fail
    Risky Operation
EXCEPT
    # Code that runs if error occurs
    Log    Error caught!
END

How It Works:

  1. Code in TRY block executes normally
  2. If an error occurs, execution jumps to EXCEPT block
  3. EXCEPT block handles the error
  4. Test continues after END (doesn't fail)
  5. If no error occurs, EXCEPT block is skipped

Example: Handling Timeout

TRY
    Log    Reading sensor data...
    Fail    Connection timeout  # Simulates error
EXCEPT
    Log    Sensor unavailable, using default value
    ${value}=    Set Variable    0
END
Log    Diagnostic continues with value: ${value}

Output: Logs "Reading sensor data...", then "Sensor unavailable, using default value", then "Diagnostic continues with value: 0". Test passes despite the Fail keyword.

⚠️ TRY/EXCEPT Rules

  • TRY block must come before EXCEPT
  • EXCEPT catches ALL errors in TRY block
  • Without TRY/EXCEPT, Fail keyword would stop the test
  • Code after END runs regardless of error
  • TRY/EXCEPT/END structure must be complete
